content_preview.title: Ladybird Ships Its First Public Alpha, Opening a From-Scratch Browser Engine to macOS and Linux Testers
content_preview.summary: Ladybird released its first downloadable alpha for macOS and Linux, nearly six months after its maintainers stopped taking public pull requests to tighten security review ahead of the launch.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Ladybird, the independent web browser built on an engine written from scratch rather than forked from Chromium, Gecko, or WebKit, released its first public alpha on November 23, according to [a post](https://ladybird.org/posts/alpha) by project founder Andreas Kling. editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (819 words, within the 400-1200 range) using the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know format. Neutral, attribution-heavy prose; every direct quote is wrapped in quotation marks and attributed inline to a named post or outlet; no editorializing and no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 6 sources from decompressed snapshots in sources/2026-11/ladybird-ships-its-first-public-alpha-opening-a-from-scratch-browser-engine-to-macos-and-linux-testers/ (source-0.html.gz through source-5.html.gz); all 6 sha256 hashes independently rehashed and match manifest.json; no suspicious_patterns flagged on any entry. source-0 (ladybird.org/download/) confirmed the page itself links to https://download.ladybird.org/releases.json labelled 'the release manifest' - this is the basis for the allowlist addition below. source-1 (download.ladybird.org/releases.json) is JSON, not HTML, and contains exactly one release: version 2026.47.7, published 2026-11-23T01:04:31Z, macOS build minimum_macos_version '14.4' - both facts verbatim-match the article. source-2 (ladybird.org/posts/alpha, dated 'Mon, 23 Nov 2026', byline Andreas Kling) verbatim-supports every one of the 8 quoted spans attributed to it ('Ladybird improves quickly...', 'Hello friends!...', 'Ladybird is a browser with a new engine...', 'The alpha is a rolling channel...'/'the part I'm most excited about', 'If you build websites...', 'This is an alpha...', 'We want security nerds to hack it!...'). source-3 (ladybird.org/posts/changing-how-we-develop-ladybird/, dated 'Fri, 05 Jun 2026') verbatim-supports every quoted span attributed to it, including 'As we work toward our first alpha release' - a first-party June confirmation that this was always planned/referred to as the project's first alpha. source-4 (linuxiac.com, byline Bobby Borisov, dated November 24, 2026) independently states Ladybird 'launches its first public alpha' and verbatim-supports the Flatpak/DEB(Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, 26.04+)/RPM(Fedora 44, 45) packaging claims and the pre-alpha feature list (file downloads, searchable history, dev tools, process sandboxing) attributed to it. source-5 (heise.de, byline Moritz Forster) independently states 'Das Ladybird-Projekt hat die erste offentliche Alpha ... veroffentlicht' (= 'has released the first public alpha') and verbatim-supports the Apple Silicon requirement, the LibWeb/LibJS engine description, and the SerenityOS-origin claim attributed to it. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article quotes Kling discussing 'AI tools' generically (no vendor named) and never names Anthropic, Claude, or an Anthropic product in the headline, summary, lead, or body.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Quote-by-quote audit against raw snapshot text: all 15 double-quoted spans in body_markdown (including the two short phrase-level quotes, 'the part I'm most excited about' and 'mountain of work ahead') are verbatim substrings of source-2 or source-3, with no paraphrase-as-quote and no misattribution. Novelty claim independently verified, not self-reported: the headline's 'first public alpha' is corroborated by three independent statements - Ladybird's own June 5 post framing the policy change as preparation 'As we work toward our first alpha release' (source-3), Linuxiac's 'launches its first public alpha' (source-4), and heise's 'die erste offentliche Alpha' (source-5) - and by releases.json listing exactly one release ever (source-1). No evidence of an earlier public alpha/beta surfaced in any source; this is not an overclaim. Duration recompute verified: the June 5, 2026 pull-request-policy post to the November 23, 2026 alpha release is 5 months 18 days, which rounds to 'nearly six months' (closer to six months than to five) - 'nearly six months' is accurate; 'five months' would have undercounted. Internal cross-reference verified: the body's link to /article/2026-11/21-ladybirds-october-update-ships-a-javascript-jit-rewrites-its-webassembly-engine-and-passes-safari-technology-preview-on-wpt resolves to an actual published article file. Derived/vendor figures: macOS 14.4 minimum and version 2026.47.7 both traced to the vendor's own releases.json and labelled as the vendor's own manifest, not asserted as Herald-derived figures.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. The 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags the absence of a Windows-build timetable and a post-alpha roadmap rather than speculating.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. Searched src/content/articles/2026-11/ for prior Ladybird coverage: only one prior article exists, 21-ladybirds-october-update-ships-a-javascript-jit-rewrites-its-webassembly-engine-and-passes-safari-technology-preview-on-wpt.md, which covers the October development update (JIT compiler, WebAssembly engine rewrite) - a distinct story from this alpha-release announcement, and the submission correctly cross-references it rather than duplicating its content. No other open PR or published article covers the November 23 alpha release.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced News item with no factual errors found across a literal quote-by-quote check of all 15 quoted spans and an independent re-verification of the 'first public alpha' novelty claim against three independent sources plus the vendor's own release manifest. The writer's two self-reported fixes (dropping an inapplicable Anthropic-disclosure sentence; recomputing the June-to-November duration from 'five months' to 'nearly six months') are both correct in the final text. The single automated warning was a missing-allowlist-entry for download.ladybird.org, resolved in this review by confirming it is the Ladybird project's own release-manifest subdomain (linked directly from ladybird.org/download/) and adding it to config/source_allowlist.txt - not a content defect, so no corrections record is warranted. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurately verified release coverage of a from-scratch browser engine reaching its first public alpha, of clear interest to web developers and the open-source browser-engine audience but not a broad-general-interest or industry-altering event.
